record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.context_brief: Weakly first-countable but not first-countable compacta
record.original_question: Using the same notion of weak first-countability given in the paper, does there exist, in ZFC, a compact space X that is weakly first-countable but not first-countable?

evidence.quote:
A space X is called weakly ﬁrst-countable if there exists
a weakly basic wf c-structure on X.

Problem 3 (Arhangel’skii, < 1978). Give an example in ZF C of a weakly ﬁrst-
countable, but not ﬁrst-countable, compact space X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a topological space. A weakly basic wfc-structure on $X$ is an assignment to each point $x\in X$ of a countable decreasing family $\{C_n(x):n\in\omega\}$ of subsets of $X$ with $x\in C_{n+1}(x)\subseteq C_n(x)$ for every $n$, such that a subset $U\subseteq X$ is open if and only if for every $x\in U$ there exists $n\in\omega$ with $C_n(x)\subseteq U$. A space $X$ is called weakly first-countable if it admits some weakly basic wfc-structure. A space $X$ is first-countable if every point has a countable neighbourhood base.

Question: Working in ZFC (without additional set-theoretic hypotheses such as CH), does there exist a compact Hausdorff space $X$ that is weakly first-countable but not first-countable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was originally posed by Arhangel'skii (before 1978), and was answered affirmatively under CH by Jakovlev (1976) and later by Malykhin (1982). A 2023 preprint/paper titled "Examples of Weakly First-Countable Compact Spaces in ZFC" claims to give ZFC examples of compact weakly first-countable spaces that are not first-countable, which would settle the problem; however, the contents could not be independently verified through the search results, so the status is reported as partially solved with a claimed ZFC resolution.

status_evidence.title: Examples of Weakly First-Countable Compact Spaces in ZFC (ResearchGate)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper title explicitly claims ZFC examples of weakly first-countable compact spaces, addressing Arhangel'skii's problem.
status_evidence.claim: A 2023 paper claims to construct ZFC examples of compact weakly first-countable non-first-countable spaces.

status_evidence.title: On Jakovlev spaces, Israel Journal of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Jakovlev (1976) constructed under CH a compact weakly first-countable space that is not first-countable; later strengthened by Malykhin (1982) under CH.
status_evidence.claim: Under CH, such compact spaces are known to exist; the ZFC version was a longstanding open problem of Arhangel'skii.
